forward.prompt:
These are the eligible OVERVIEW photographs of one clothing SKU. Detail/closeup photographs have been excluded. Each VIEW contains its original photograph and SAM3 mask regions.
R001, R002, etc. are UNIQUE addresses of pixels, NOT garment identities. Different views ALWAYS have different region IDs. Match the clothing visually across those DIFFERENT IDs. Never require an ID to repeat across views.
Find each visually distinct garment with at least one usable region in EVERY shown VIEW. One garment may occupy MULTIPLE SAM3 masks in one view and ONE mask in another. A dress's bodice, waist panel, sleeves and attached skirt are parts of the SAME dress, not separate garments merely because SAM3 split them. A seam, change of transparency, pose or front/back appearance does not establish a different garment. Use the full photographs to identify construction and physical garment extent. In contrast, a separately visible shirt under a vest/jacket remains a distinct visual layer, even if sewn together. Matching color alone is insufficient. Mixed masks are not usable.
Only a visible portion is required in an overview; do not require full silhouettes. Keep repeated styling too when present in every shown view. Do not select by the item for sale. Do not invent new mask boundaries.
Return JSON only: {"reason":"brief visual comparison", "tracks":[{"garment":"description", "regions":["R001", "R004"]}]}. The IDs here are schema examples, not an answer. Each track must list actual supplied IDs covering EVERY shown VIEW, including all confirmed parts of that garment. Assign a region to at most one track. Unlisted regions are removed. If no garment is visibly supported everywhere, return an empty tracks list.

Thus, the cargo pant (R001/R003) and the utility/tailored pant (R002/R004) are two distinct garments, each appearing in both views. No other garments are consistently visible across both views.", "tracks": [{"garment": "black cargo-style pant with elastic waist and side pocket", "regions": ["R001", "R003"]}, {"garment": "black utility/tailored pant with buttoned pockets and structured waist", "regions": ["R002", "R004"]}]}

all_view_rule: Every eligible overview must support a visible part of the same garment. Closeups are excluded from both matching and context. No full silhouette is required.

identity.prompt:
Classify this retail photograph by its photographic composition, NOT by the clothing category or whether the full person is visible.
OVERVIEW: a normal front/back/side outfit or garment view, or a product-only photograph showing the overall object. A headless model, cropped legs, partial occlusion, or a small accessory filling the image does not by itself make a detail shot. A complete product photograph is an overview.
CLOSEUP: a deliberate tight detail shot of only a garment subsection, such as fabric, neckline, shoulder/back opening, fastener, label, waist or hem. The overall garment extent is outside the frame. These detail photographs are excluded from a later matching task.
UNCERTAIN: you cannot distinguish these photographic roles. Never guess based on file names or an item's title.
Return only JSON: {"role":"overview|closeup|uncertain", "reason":"brief explanation of the visible framing"}. Choose exactly one role.

The framing includes the full length of each garment from waist to hem, with no focus on specific details or subsections, indicating a complete product photograph."}

explanation.reason: The image displays two full pairs of pants in their entirety, positioned side by side against a neutral background. region_comparisons.prompt:
The earlier images show all eligible OVERVIEW photographs of the SAME SKU (closeups excluded) for context. The final TWO cards are the ONLY mask regions being compared. Each card has outlined source context on the left and EXACT MASK PIXELS on the right. Identify the garment underneath those exact pixels, not other clothes elsewhere in the photographs.
Do the two exact mask regions show parts of ONE SAME visually distinct garment? Any identifiable visible part counts: fabric detail, tie, strap, collar, sleeve, hem or partly hidden strip. Full silhouettes and equal visible extents are NEVER required. Use the other photographs to link a detail to its garment. A dress's bodice, waist, sleeves and attached skirt are parts of ONE garment even when isolated masks have different shapes. Identify the whole garment from the source photographs before comparing its masked parts; do not call its upper and lower sections different garments. A transparent panel or waist seam alone does not separate garments. Two separate garments or layers remain DIFFERENT even if their colors match or they are sewn together. Background, mixed masks and uncertain identity must not be joined. A white shirt does not match a black skirt simply because both clothes appear elsewhere in the context photographs. Compare ONLY the two given masks; do not choose alternative regions.
Return JSON only: {"region1":"actual mask contents", "region2":"actual mask contents", "reason":"visual identity comparison", "verdict":"A"}.
Each description must be under 12 words, reason under 25 words. A means SAME garment (including a visible part); B means DIFFERENT garment/object/background; C means uncertain or mixed. The A in the schema is an example, not an answer.
region_comparisons.raw: {"region1":"black tailored trousers with back pockets and belt loops", "region2":"black cargo trousers with side pockets and drawstring waist", "reason":"Different cut, pocket style, and waist closure; one tailored, one cargo-style", "verdict":"B"}

explanation.region1: black tailored trousers with back pockets and belt loops
explanation.region2: black cargo trousers with side pockets and drawstring waist
explanation.reason: Different cut, pocket style, and waist closure; one tailored, one cargo-style
